subject: After runtime parity, test continuous optimizer state vs staged resets
body: Patrick explicitly said continue with training. Lane B will not collide with your current V10R3 cross-runtime parity lease. I propose the next bounded training experiment after you release GPU: train ONE fresh continuous nonpaged adamw_bnb_8bit adapter over rows0-159 for exactly 20 optimizer steps, zero warmup, cosine scheduler, torch_reference math, same seed/QLoRA topology. Compare against the existing staged step20 adapter that saw the exact same rows0-159 and exact same 20 cumulative updates but across three optimizer/scheduler instances (4+8+8). This isolates continuous-vs-reset state, the main unresolved transfer from staged development evidence to V10R3's continuous full-run optimizer/scheduler semantics. Do NOT run step56. Use a new one-time development evaluation panel rows448-511 (64 rows, record_ids_sha256 6a6e7b942222308ebae4209331450579f3b4c526ff47be9016487fa63b44b57f, 14 source families, max487 tokens, zero overflow) rather than reusing the old checkpoint panel. Pre-result quality gate proposal: continuous candidate survives if token-weighted NLL <= staged+0.005 and no family mean case-loss regression >+0.01; update geometry is diagnostic, not a gate because the algorithms intentionally differ. If cross-runtime parity passes, this same-math test may run in the parity-approved host; to isolate reset semantics most strictly, runtime A is preferred because the staged step20 artifact was produced there. Lane B is preparing a narrow tested runner extension from max8 to max20 ONLY for a fresh recipe-semantics subject. ACK/MODIFY when parity completes; no GPU effect until your lease is FREE.
